dossier.valuation_method: NAV + probability-weighted, time-discounted rNPV of pipeline (composite of event branches, explicit royalty curve), net of financing dilution; science-contingent pre-revenue biotech
dossier.thesis_summary: Anixa is an asset-light, pre-revenue oncology developer = ~$12.8M net liquid assets (~$0.38/sh, essentially all Treasuries/MMF) plus the risk-adjusted value of an in-licensed pipeline it intends to out-license to pharma. The off-the-shelf alpha-lactalbumin TNBC vaccine (Phase 1 complete, all endpoints met, 74% immune response, DoD-funded) drives ~45% of expected value; ovarian CAR-T lira-cel and the AMHR2 ovarian vaccine are smaller, earlier, lower-probability options. Probability-weighted FMV ~$0.74/share vs ~$0.38 net-cash floor; distribution is right-skewed/bimodal, governed by single-digit success probabilities in cancer vaccines and solid-tumor CAR-T. At ~$2.70 the stock implies ~73% downside; recommendation AVOID/underweight. NOLs (~$175M) near-worthless (100% valuation allowance + Section 382); insiders own only ~5% in real shares amid ~4.3%/yr option dilution and a ~$40-50M Phase 2 financing gap.
key_value_drivers: Breast-cancer vaccine PoS (central 6%) and peak sales / net royalty after Cleveland Clinic/Wistar pass-through (explicit royalty curve: ~$540M royalties + ~$60-110M milestones at launch)
Net liquid assets (~$14.2M) and cash-burn/dilution (~$7M/yr, ~2yr runway, ~4.3%/yr option dilution + $100M ATM; ~$40-50M Phase 2 financing gap)
Out-license economics; single-asset Phase-1/2 cancer-vaccine comps ~$20-55M upfront + biobucks + high-single-to-mid-teens royalties
Free/subsidized development via DoD (breast Phase 1) and NCI PREVENT (ovarian vaccine)
Solid-tumor CAR-T lira-cel optionality (low probability, zero approved precedent)
key_risks: Cancer vaccines ~1 approval ever (Provenge); immunogenicity is not efficacy; no preventative-endpoint precedent
Solid-tumor CAR-T zero approvals ever; lira-cel efficacy anecdotal at sub-therapeutic doses
~2 years cash; ~1.4M options/yr (~4.3%) + ATM dilution; ~40% option overhang; ~$40-50M Phase 2 funding gap
Anixa holds licenses only and shares upside with Cleveland Clinic/Wistar
Heavily promoted small-float name with short-squeeze/catalyst-pop risk; insiders own only ~5% in real shares
NOLs (~$175M) near-worthless due to 100% valuation allowance + undetermined Section 382 limitation
what_would_change_my_mind: Phase 2 clinical efficacy (not just immune response) for the breast vaccine
A pharma partnership with disclosed upfront/milestone/royalty economics
Objective RECIST responses for lira-cel at therapeutic doses
Non-dilutive (grant/partner) funding of the breast Phase 2
A deeply dilutive financing or program discontinuation (downside)

Central peak-sales of $1.5B is a single-point estimate doing meaningful work in the success branch — fully sensitivity-tested, but a fuller treatment might probability-weight the peak itself
